## Metadata

- Bug ID: investigate-chain-input-contracts-defect-report
- Reporter: the operator, through a supplied defect report
- Severity: high
- Status: provisional

## Symptom Summary

- Observed behavior: A phase whose predecessor has completed stays blocked at guard G5-INPUT with "no accepted input type supplied", because the artifact the runtime hands over carries an identifier the consuming agent does not list. The blocked phase leaves its successors pending, so the run cannot finish. The defect is wider than reported: 13 of 29 consecutive hand-offs across 6 workflows offer an identifier the consumer does not accept, and 4 of 7 profile routing rows name an entry input the entry agent rejects.
- Expected behavior: Each phase accepts the artifact its Phase Model Input column names from the phase before it, and the profile routes each command with an input type its entry agent accepts, as stated by the operator in the defect report (`E-001`).
- First observed date: Not established. Reproduced in this run on 2026-10-09; the earliest committed evidence read is a stalled investigate run that predates this analysis.
- Affected environments: Known affected is the framework tree of this working copy at runtime 0.9.0, reproduced in a throwaway mirror. Known unaffected, by measurement, are the refactor chain and the fix-bug chain when the entry input type persists in the pool. Not observed are the main checkout, the bundled payload copy, and consumer repositories with their own framework copies.

- Preconditions: A tree identical to this working copy, mirrored to a scratch location outside the repository so no committed run evidence is touched. (4) Repeat step 3 with problem-statement and investigation-question both supplied and read the same phase. (5) Run the measurement scripts, which compute every hand-off from the manifests and the Phase Models using the runtime's own contract functions.

## Impact Assessment

- User impact: An operator running the investigate, research, review-pull-request, or release command cannot finish the run without foreknowledge of the guard: investigate and research always stop at 3 phases; the others stop at 1 or 2 unless the right extra type was supplied up front. Operators of fix-bug, refactor, and the code-quality scan are not affected.
- Business impact: No business impact statement was supplied; severity rests on technical impact alone and the question is routed to the product owner.
- Technical impact: Correctness of the framework's own contract: 13 of 29 declared hand-offs are undispatchable under G5-INPUT although the framework declares every phase dispatchable, and 4 of 7 profile rows cannot start a run. A stalled run also fails the self-hosting completion rule. No wrong result is produced and no data is lost; the failure is a visible block, with a workaround that needs advance knowledge and mislabels an input (`E-013`).
- Blast radius: The runtime guard and upstream hand-off path; the agent manifests and registry records of planner, architect, context-agent, tech-lead, documentation, and reviewer as consumers of blocked hand-offs and business-analyst, reviewer, and tech-lead as entry agents of rejected profile rows; the Phase Models of five workflows (investigate, research, review-pull-request, release, and implement-feature when entered through a type the architect does not accept); the self-hosting profile routing table and its router; the self-hosting verifier through stalled runs; the bundled payload mirror of all of these; consumer repositories holding framework copies, not observed. Persisted bad data: the committed stalled investigate run, which holds three completed artifacts and two pending phases and fails the completion rule while it stays on disk.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Root cause statement: Producer output identifiers and consumer accepted-input identifiers are declared independently with no authoritative mapping from a Phase Model Input column to an identifier, so the runtime offers each artifact under a name that the consuming agents' contracts at 13 hand-offs do not list, and the profile independently names entry types no entry agent lists.
- Why detection failed earlier: Manifest, registry, and Phase Model verifiers check each agent or table alone and no check composes a Phase Model edge with the producer's output and the consumer's accepted list; the one earlier repair of this class recorded the per-edge check as deliberately deferred and left thirteen mismatches, and the profile's input types were never tested against the entry agent.

### Causal Chain

| ID | Step | Claim | Evidence | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C-001` | Independent declarations | Each manifest declares its output and accepted identifiers on its own, and the Phase Model Input column names files, so nothing ties a hand-off to an accepted identifier | `E-004`, `E-011` | high |
| `C-002` | Offer under producer name | The runtime offers the upstream artifact under the producing manifest's output identifier, or the file stem | `E-002` | high |
| `C-003` | Guard narrows and requires a listed type | G5-INPUT discards types the consumer does not declare and, for a menu contract, requires one accepted type; optional-only types do not count | `E-003` | high |
| `C-004` | Mismatch at 13 edges | For 13 of 29 consecutive hand-offs the offered identifier is absent from the consumer's accepted list, in one case (execution-plan at the architect) only optional | `E-005`, `E-011`, `E-014` | high |
| `C-005` | Supplied inputs rescue only some chains | Entry-supplied types survive into later pools and rescue fix-bug, refactor, and some implement-feature edges, but no entry type of investigate or research is accepted by the later consumers | `E-006`, `E-009`, `E-013` | high |
| `C-006` | Profile entry mismatch | Four of seven profile rows name a sole entry input the entry agent rejects, an independent instance of the same missing mapping | `E-007`, `E-012` | high |
| `C-007` | Observed block | The consuming phase blocks at G5-INPUT with the accepted list in its reason, its successors stay pending, and the run stalls | `E-008`, `E-010` | high |

## Fix Strategy

- Proposed fix: Make every Phase Model hand-off deliver the upstream artifact under an identifier the consuming agent accepts, for all 13 mismatched edges and not only the four reported, and make each profile row name an entry type its entry agent accepts, while an input type no agent accepts is still rejected. The change is conditional on the architect settling where the mapping lives, which also decides version and registry changes (`E-015`). Add an automated check over every declared workflow edge and profile route that needs no model. The committed stalled run stays untouched; its disposition is a gate-owner decision.
- Alternative options: Declare the upstream identifiers in each consuming manifest, which changes agent versions and registry records and widens each accepted menu; or add one runtime mapping from an output identifier to an accepted abstract type, which is one change but adds a rule the manifests do not state; or require operators to supply the extra types up front, which hides the defect and mislabels inputs and is not recommended.
- Regression risk: high
- Regression scope: Every workflow whose hand-offs are changed, because guard G5-INPUT is shared by all phases; the sibling pools already passing, such as refactor and fix-bug, because widening an accepted menu changes what narrowing keeps; manifest versions and registry records because the loader compares them; the bundled payload mirror because it copies the same files; the verifiers and tests that pin the profile table and the accepted menus.

## Validation Plan

- Verification steps: In a scratch mirror, repeat the reproduction with the same single entry type per workflow and confirm that every consecutive hand-off of investigate and research, and of the other three affected workflows, passes G5-INPUT once its predecessor's artifact is committed, that each profile row plans without a block at the entry phase, and that a supplied type no agent declares is still rejected.
- Regression tests added: A per-edge test over every active workflow that composes the Phase Model edge, the producer's output identifier, and the consumer's accepted list with the real contract function; a profile test that plans each routing row's entry types against the entry agent; a negative test for an undeclared type; and a producer-existence check for accepted identifiers that are not operator request types.
- Monitoring signals after release: Any run whose work item is blocked at G5-INPUT with the reason awaiting a dependency output after its predecessor completed; the count of blocked hand-offs from the edge test, expected to be zero.

## Closure

- Resolution summary: None identified.
- Linked PR and release: None identified.
- Prevention actions: Run the per-edge and profile-route checks as part of manifest and registry verification so a producer or consumer identifier cannot change alone.

## Impact Assessment

- User impact: An operator running investigate or research cannot finish the run without foreknowledge of the guard: both always stop at 3 hand-offs, and both profile routes block at entry. Operators of review-pull-request, release, and implement-feature are affected at the out-of-scope edges; operators of fix-bug, refactor, and the code-quality scan are not affected (`E-006`, `E-027`).
- Business impact: No business impact statement was supplied; severity rests on technical impact alone and the question is routed to the product owner.
- Technical impact: Correctness of the framework's own contract: 13 of 29 declared hand-offs and 4 of 7 profile rows are undispatchable although every phase is declared dispatchable, and a stalled run fails the self-hosting completion rule (`E-010`, `E-028`). No wrong result and no data loss; the block is visible, and its workaround mislabels an input (`E-013`). The performance skill was triggered by the word profile in the self-hosting profile; the only performance effect found is one more upstream artifact read by each recommendation phase under the recommended change (`E-031`).
- Blast radius: The G5-INPUT guard and the hand-off path; the input contracts of context-agent, tech-lead, and documentation as consumers in scope, and of planner, architect, bug-analyst, reviewer, tech-lead, and documentation at out-of-scope edges; business-analyst, reviewer, and tech-lead as entry agents of rejected profile rows; the Phase Models of investigate, research, review-pull-request, release, and implement-feature; the self-hosting profile and router; the self-hosting verifier through stalled runs; registry records, host registrations, and gate precedent through agent and workflow versions (`E-015`, `E-019`, `E-020`); the bundled payload mirror; consumer framework copies, not observed. Persisted bad data: committed run run-437e2f765e4b, holding three completed artifacts, a blocked recommendation, and a pending publication, which fails the completion rule and would be rewritten by any re-evaluation once repaired (`E-034`).

## Root Cause Analysis

- Root cause statement: The consuming agents' accepted-input contracts, which each agent enforces again in its own first reasoning stage, were declared without reference to the Phase Model edges that feed them, so the context agent names the framing output by two identifiers nothing produces, tech-lead's recommendation phases are routed only an artifact its contract does not name, documentation's contract defines no input for the findings publication it owns, and the profile names entry types the entry agent does not accept, with no check composing a Phase Model edge with the producer's identifier and the consumer's contract.
- Why detection failed earlier: Registry coverage check C6 evaluates only the capability and context guards and never G5-INPUT; verify_manifests reads only write scopes and example pointers; self-hosting check S2 resolves each row's command, workflow, and entry phase but never tests its Required Inputs against the entry agent (`E-033`). The per-edge and producer-existence checks were deliberately deferred by the earlier refactor repair because they failed on arrival, not because the design rejected them (`E-014`, `E-017`). No check compares a host registration's stated version with its manifest, which is how the earlier repair's version drift survived (`E-020`).

### Causal Chain

| ID | Step | Claim | Evidence | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C-001` | Independent declarations | Each consumer's accepted list is its own reasoning contract and was written without the Phase Model: the context agent names the framing output by producerless identifiers, tech-lead is routed only its own output, documentation defines no findings input | `E-004`, `E-011`, `E-021`, `E-022`, `E-023`, `E-024`, `E-025` | high |
| `C-002` | Offer under producer name | The runtime offers the upstream artifact under the producing manifest's output identifier; delivery uses the un-narrowed pool, the guard the narrowed one | `E-002`, `E-026` | high |
| `C-003` | Guard narrows and requires a listed type | G5-INPUT discards types the consumer does not declare and requires one accepted type; optional-only types do not count; the loader couples manifest and registry versions | `E-003`, `E-015` | high |
| `C-004` | Mismatch at 13 edges | 13 of 29 hand-offs offer an identifier the consumer does not accept, 6 of them in investigate and research; the earlier repair fixed one edge the same way and left the rest | `E-005`, `E-014`, `E-018`, `E-028` | high |
| `C-005` | Supplied inputs rescue only some chains | Entry types persist into later pools and rescue fix-bug and refactor, but no entry type of investigate or research is accepted downstream without mislabelling | `E-006`, `E-009`, `E-013` | high |
| `C-006` | Profile entry mismatch | Two in-scope rows name investigation-request, declared by nothing, and research-question, optional only to the entry agent, whose contract names problem-statement as the input of these runs | `E-007`, `E-012`, `E-027` | high |
| `C-007` | Observed block | The consuming phase blocks at G5-INPUT with the accepted list in its reason, its successors stay pending, and the run stalls and fails the completion rule | `E-008`, `E-010`, `E-027` | high |

## Fix Strategy

- Proposed fix: Make each in-scope consumer's contract state the artifact its Phase Model edge delivers, in the place that consumer's own contract already points, and make the two in-scope profile rows name the entry type the entry agent defines for these runs; the guard code stays unchanged and keeps rejecting any type the consumer does not declare (`E-030`, `E-032`). Entry inputs: decision-support and external-research name problem-statement (`E-012`). Hand-offs: the context agent accepts requirement-framing in place of framed-objective and research-brief, which denote that same framing output and were never supplied (`E-022`); the recommendation and recommendation-draft rows' Input column also names investigation-report.md, the evidence base tech-lead's unchanged contract already accepts, so tech-lead gains no input and keeps its version (`E-023`, `E-031`); documentation accepts technical-recommendation for the findings basis of its two publication phases, and its lifecycle table names technical-recommendation.md for them (`E-024`). Every surface that states a changed contract changes with it, as in the earlier repair: minimum-satisfaction and identity text, the context agent's sourceInputs vocabulary and its report template comment, registry data dependencies, version 1.1.0 for both agents in manifest, registry, and host registration with contractVersion held, the investigate and research workflow versions under their additive rule, and the bundled payload synced by its own command (`E-018`, `E-020`, `E-036`). No runtime module or runtime version changes. The committed stalled run is not re-evaluated as part of the fix; its disposition stays with the gate owner (`E-034`).
- Alternative options: (A for all three consumers) also add technical-recommendation to tech-lead's menu: tech-lead would accept its own output as an evidence base in all six of its phases, needing a third version move and resetting Merge and Readiness Gate precedent (`E-019`, `E-023`). (B) A runtime alias from an output identifier to an accepted type works only for the context agent; tech-lead and documentation accept nothing corresponding, so an alias would mislabel the artifact (`E-013`, `E-024`). (C) Letting an Input-column edge artifact satisfy G5-INPUT passes 28 of 29 edges with no version change, but it dispatches agents whose own first stage still refuses the input, moving the block into a charged attempt; it makes G5 equal to the predecessor guard at every such edge, rests on fuzzy term matching, and silently changes 6 out-of-scope hand-offs, so it is weaker than the status quo (`E-021`, `E-029`). (D) Per-phase menus in manifests restate the Phase Model's per-phase facts in a second place, a schema and runtime change that recreates the independent-declaration condition; it stays architect's structural question (`E-017`, `E-019`). (E) Profile-only repair rescues the context agent with an extra raw question but needs mislabelled types for tech-lead and documentation (`E-009`, `E-013`).
- Regression risk: medium
- Regression scope: Documentation's three other phases (implement-feature documentation-and-release-handoff, review-pull-request documentation-impact, release communication-and-post-release), through its agent-global menu: a technical-recommendation in their pools now satisfies it, though pools today carry only edge artifacts and operator inputs (`E-026`, `E-030`). The context agent's two phases, through withdrawal of two identifiers no run supplied (`E-022`). The investigate and research dependency graphs, parallel groups, and dispatch payloads, through the added Input-column edge into each recommendation phase (`E-031`). Gate auto-approval precedent for the investigate and research gates and for gates assessing documentation's output, through the workflow and agent version keys (`E-019`, `E-036`). The loader's manifest-to-registry version check and the two host registrations' stated version (`E-015`, `E-020`). Registry data dependencies in registry/agents.yaml. The bundled payload parity test, through six mirrored files (`E-033`). The two profile routes and self-hosting check S2. The committed stalled run, through the scheduler re-evaluation pass (`E-034`). The 7 out-of-scope hand-offs and two profile rows keep their verdicts (`E-030`).

## Validation Plan

- Verification steps: In a throwaway mirror of the repaired tree, repeat the reproduction with problem-statement as the only supplied input: every phase of investigate and research passes G5-INPUT once its predecessor's artifact is committed, the router names problem-statement for both rows, and planning with investigation-request or research-question still blocks at entry. Reach the condition, not only the symptom: at each of the six in-scope hand-offs the delivered artifact survives narrowing under an identifier the consumer's contract accepts, the per-edge count falls from 13 to 7 with every remaining block out of scope, and the 16 hand-offs that passed before still pass. Read the edited surfaces and confirm each states the same accepted set and the same versions.
- Regression tests added: One new contract module, run without a model, failing before the repair and passing after: a per-edge test over every active workflow composing derive_dependencies, the producer's output identifier as the lease records it, narrow_inputs, and resolve_input_contract, asserting a pass except for an explicit set of the seven out-of-scope edges, each asserted still to fail so the set must shrink as follow-ups land; named tests for each investigate and research hand-off; a profile-route test asserting the entry agent's contract is satisfiable from the decision-support and external-research Required Inputs, with change-review and framework-release held as known gaps; negative tests for investigation-request and research-question at the business analyst, framed-objective and research-brief at the context agent, technical-recommendation alone at tech-lead, and an empty pool at documentation; and a version agreement test across manifest, registry record, and host registration for the two changed agents.
- Monitoring signals after release: Work items blocked at G5-INPUT with reason awaiting_dependency_output whose predecessors are all completed, expected zero for investigate and research; the known-gap count of the per-edge test, expected seven and falling; any investigate or research dispatch whose agent raises an input error in its first stage while G5-INPUT passed, expected zero.

## Closure

- Resolution summary: None identified.
- Linked PR and release: None identified.
- Prevention actions: Ship the per-edge and profile-route checks with explicit, self-shrinking known-gap sets so they pass on arrival; add a version agreement check between manifest, registry record, and host registration; route extending registry coverage C6 or self-hosting S2 to report G5-INPUT as a follow-up.

input_contract.minimum_satisfaction: At least one accepted input must be present. It supplies the accepted change this agent implements: a technical design for feature work, a bug analysis for a defect fix, or the safety-net validation report for a behaviour-preserving refactor, which is the artifact the refactor workflow's own predecessor phase publishes. Without one there is no accepted change, and implementing anyway would mean designing.

repositoryWrites.rationale: This is the only framework role that changes repository source. Its write scope cannot be enumerated per agent, because the files a change touches are named by the accepted design rather than by the manifest. The scope is therefore the repository, minus the evidence classes below, and every file actually written is declared in the change set and in the result envelope, where the runtime compares them.
repositoryWrites.exclusionRationale: Committed run evidence and governance records are immutable to the agents whose work they record. A run artifact this agent could edit would let a change rewrite the evidence assessed against it.

determinism.contract: Identical approved inputs and an identical context snapshot must produce the same change-set entry set, the same test-evidence set, the same deviation set, and the same declared verification status.
determinism.orderingRule: Change-set entries are ordered by the sequence in which the accepted design requires them; ties break toward the lower path in lexical order. Test-evidence entries follow the change-set entries they cover.
determinism.modelIndependence: No module may reference a specific model, vendor, or agent runtime. Technology names are permitted only when they trace to the supplied design, standards, or repository context.
